Commentary.Commentary: 256 to win then. Have Bangladesh got enough to counter the dew? Will the pitch get some pace with the ball skidding on? But then, turn will come into play as well. Interesting questions. Join us back at 5.15 pm local (1115 GMT).

To be honest, Windies did not bowl badly. Keemo Paul was expensive and so was Oshane Thomas but the latter came back well towards the end, with 3 wickets overall. Roach was frugal while Devendra Bishoo was the pick of the bowlers, with just 1/27 in his 10 overs.

It was Mahmudullah's wicket in the 41st over which put the brakes on the scoring. Just 64 runs came in the final 10 overs for the loss of 4 wickets. Some excellent death overs' bowling and usage of slower balls cramped Bangladesh as they just kept swinging early.

Around the 24th over, the hosts lost Tamim and immediately Rahim followed. However, any chance of a comeback was thwarted as Mahmudullah and Shakib counter-attacked. The latter was more on the attack and was taking the game away but the death overs proved to be fatal for the Men In Green.

Hmmm... a mixed bag of an innings for the home side. They started cautiously, but then Tamim and Rahim started to go big. Their 111-run stand gave Bangladesh dreams of around 300 but loss in concentration came in between.

Bangladesh lose their first wicket but technically they are 2 down. Just the start Windies would have wanted.
Bowls a bouncer, Kayes  does well to duck under it.
Good length delivery on off, Kayes defends off the front foot.
On a good length around off, Tamim defends solidly.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Full and wide outside off, Kayes looks to drive but misses. Shai Hope behind tries to stop it by closing his legs but the ball deflects off his pads to fine leg. A bye taken.
Full and outside off, probably the off cutter, Tamim drives it through mid off for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a good length outside off, coming in sharply, Tamim looks to defend but gets squared up. Is hit on the back thigh.
Good length delivery on middle, Kayes defends from within the crease.
Wide outside off, Kayes looks to drive but misses it and gets beaten on this one. Ultra Edge shows there was no nick on it.
Bowls full on middle, Tamim flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
Imrul Kayes walks in now.

Das is down on the ground. The physio is out in the middle. In fact, DAS IS BEING STRETCHERED OFF THE FIELD. Not great news at all. Get the feeling that he got hit on the shin, just below the ankle and maybe the contact was with the bone. OUCH.
LEG BYE! Full on leg, the batsman looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. Liton is not looking comfortable and is down in pain. The batsmen however cross ends.
Full on middle, Das flicks it to mid-wicket.
FREE HIT! FOUR! Length delivery on off, Das makes room and lofts it over covers for a boundary.
NO BALL! Oshane oversteps. Length delivery on leg, Tamim flicks it towards fine leg. The batsmen take a run.
Oshane Thomas to bowl with the second new ball.
Full on middle, Tamim flicks it towards mid on for a single.
Full again on middle, the batsman flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full on middle, Liton flicks it to mid-wicket.
Again on a good length delivery on off, Das blocks it well.
Good length delivery on off, Das plays it towards the bowler.
Length delivery on middle, Tamim flicks it towards square leg. The batsmen take a run.
WIDE! Roach starts with a wide. Bowls down the leg side, Tamim lets it go.
The players are out in the middle. Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das are the openers. Kemar Roach to start off proceedings to Tamim, Here we go...

Bangladesh captain, Mashrafe Mortaza, says that there is plenty of variation in his bowling side and it did well in the last match. is looking forward to this one and hopes that his side bats well today. On being informed about the quintet featuring in 100 ODIs together (Himself, Rahim, Tamim, Shakib and Mahmudullah), Mashrafe says that there are plenty of memories, not possible to remember all but adds that they have enjoyed a lot playing together and Bangladesh cricket has come a long way forward.

Windies skipper, Rovman Powell, says that the decision is based due to the dew as the ball comes better onto the bat in the evening. Informs that Kieran Powell misses out today and young Chandrapaul Hemraj replaces him. Is not too worried about the last match loss and says that the guys just need to keep working on small areas. Says that he intends to use himself and Samuels while bowling.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Mortaza spins it, Heads is the call and it is HEADS. WINDIES OPT TO CHASE.
PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo observes that it is a good surface and there are runs to be scored here. There will be true bounce and turn.

Hello and welcome to the 2nd ODI between Bangladesh and Windies at Mirpur. The hosts have started confidently and will look to seal the series today itself. On the other hand, the visitors have to come good with the bat. The openers need to give a solid start upfront so that the other batsmen don't crumble under pressure. Chase and Paul came good in the last match and the visitors will learn from their batting and do well in this match. This is a do-or-die match for them. The hosts would also like to improve their batting and Tamim Iqbal's form is crucial for them. At the same time, the home side would also like to improve their bowling in the death overs. What's in store for us? Stay tuned.
